dmaria-ii.name: D. Maria II Secondary School
dmaria-ii.short: A 1964 girls’ lyceum; boys joined in 1973, and it became a secondary school in 1974
dmaria-ii.long: The D. Maria II Lyceum was created in Braga in spring 1964 as a girls’ lyceum with 24 classrooms. In its first year it took 1,014 pupils. Boys were admitted in 1973, and after the 1974 revolution it became a secondary school. In its first half-century, more than 80,000 people studied here.
dmaria-ii.history:
Decree-Law 45636 of 31 March 1964 created the D. Maria II National Lyceum in Braga. The decree describes it as “a girls’ lyceum with 24 classrooms”. The school is named after Queen Maria II (1819–1853). Its address today is Rua 25 de Abril, 198, a few minutes’ walk from the historic centre.

In the first school year, 1,014 girls attended day classes. Single-sex teaching lasted until 1973, when the education reform of minister Veiga Simão opened the lyceum to boys. By 1974 there were already 1,911 pupils in mixed classes. After the revolution of 25 April 1974, the lyceum was renamed D. Maria II Secondary School, the name it still bears.

The busiest years came after the revolution. In 1975/76 the day classes had 2,703 pupils, and in 1981/82, counting evening classes, the total reached 2,885. More than 80,000 people studied here in the first 50 years. General courses that prepare pupils for university have always been the school’s core. Since 2005 it has also offered vocational secondary courses, and later it added evening classes for adults.

The school later became the head of the D. Maria II school group, which also includes the Lamaçães basic school. In 2014 the group had about 3,200 pupils. The state company Parque Escolar rebuilt the school in depth. The contractor put up new blocks for laboratories, workshops, a library, a sports hall and an auditorium, and renovated the older buildings. Work went ahead in phases so that the school never closed.
facts: The lyceum was created by Decree-Law 45636 of 31 March 1964.
The decree set it up as a girls’ lyceum with 24 classrooms.
Boys were admitted in 1973, after minister Veiga Simão’s reform.
It has carried its current name, D. Maria II Secondary School, since 1974.
More than 80,000 people studied here in its first 50 years.
dmaria-ii.tip: This is a working school, and visitors cannot go inside. You can see the buildings from Rua 25 de Abril, about a 10-minute walk from Praça da República.
